## Overview

This PR adds an opt-in `KernelConfig.lm_head_quantization` option for RDNA (ROCm gfx11/gfx12). With `"int4_per_group_32"`, an unquantized fp16/bf16 lm_head is quantized while the model loads:

- asymmetric uint4 weights;
- one scale and zero point per 32 input channels.

The quantized lm_head runs on the existing RDNA hybrid W4A16 op (`rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply`): `wvSplitK_int4_g` for decode (up to 5 tokens) and the Triton W4A16 kernel for prefill.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --kernel-config '{"lm_head_quantization": "int4_per_group_32"}'
```

**Why.** Decode reads the whole lm_head every step. Many int4 checkpoints keep it in full precision, so on bandwidth-bound RDNA GPUs it becomes one of the largest per-token costs. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Quark UINT4 group 128) is one example:

- Its 248320 × 2048 fp16 lm_head is about 970 MB, read every token: 4.5 ms at 211 GB/s on Strix Halo (gfx1151), the largest single item in decode.
- llama.cpp's Q4_K_M GGUF of the same model stores it as Q6_K.

Quantizing at load time needs no new checkpoint and no new kernel.

**Design.**

- **New method:** `Int4LMHeadMethod` (`quantization/online/int4_lm_head.py`) creates the weight like `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, so checkpoint loading does not change. In `process_weights_after_loading` it:
  - quantizes the weight in row chunks, which bounds the fp32 working set;
  - widens each group's range to include 0;
  - writes the codes in the layout `wvSplitK_int4_g` expects (ExLlama-shuffled int4, padded off the vector-cache cliff on gfx1151);
  - writes packed zero points `[N/8, K/32]`.
- **Shared layout code:** `pack_skinny_int4` is split, so `skinny_int4_layout` (the gfx1151 padding step) can be reused on already-shuffled weights.
- **Hook:** `ParallelLMHead` calls `_maybe_quantize_lm_head` only when no quant method was preselected, so the drafter lm_head copies made by `quantized_lm_head_copy` are not affected. The method class is imported lazily.
- **Tied embeddings:** `replace_parameter` rebinds only the lm_head's `weight`, so tied input embeddings keep their full-precision weight. An untied head frees its fp16 weight; a tied head adds the int4 copy (about 0.29 GB at this size) on top of the shared embedding.
- **Errors:** the option raises `ValueError` when it can't apply:
  - a GPU other than gfx11/gfx12;
  - an lm_head that is already quantized;
  - a `head_dtype` different from the model dtype;
  - LoRA;
  - a vocab shard not divisible by 8, or a hidden size not divisible by 32.

  It never falls back silently. The default (`None`) changes nothing.

## Claims

Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, 40 CUs, LPDDR5X about 211 GB/s), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Quark UINT4-G128 (fp16 lm_head, 248320 × 2048). Decode benchmark: 512 input / 512 output tokens, batch size 1, greedy, `ignore_eos`, median of 5 runs after 3 warmups, CUDA graphs on (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`).

| MoE backend | lm_head | TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Triton (default) | fp16 | 29.76 | 33.6 | |
| Triton (default) | **int4 g32 (this PR)** | **26.66** | **37.5** | −3.10 ms, 1.12x |
| `rdna3_w4a8` ([#62480](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62480)) | fp16 | 20.69 | 48.3 | |
| `rdna3_w4a8` ([#62480](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62480)) | **int4 g32 (this PR)** | **17.50** | **57.1** | −3.19 ms, 1.18x |

- **Saving vs bandwidth math:** the measured 3.1 to 3.2 ms/token saving matches the expected value. The lm_head read drops from about 970 MB to about 300 MB per token, about 3.2 ms at 211 GB/s.
- **Weight memory:** 18.51 GiB → 17.87 GiB.
- **Run variance:** in the combined run, 4 of 5 runs were 17.47 to 17.53 ms; one outlier at 19.53 ms doesn't change the median.
- **llama.cpp reference:** llama.cpp (Q4_K_M, `llama-bench` tg512) measures 17.82 ms on the same machine. The combined configuration is the first vLLM setup to match it on this model.

**Accuracy:** GSM8K is unchanged within noise. There is a small token-level cost, measured below.

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_int4_lm_head.py`

- CPU:
  - quantization error is at most one step, with a bounded RMS error (fp16 and bf16);
  - zero-point packing round-trips;
  - the packed layout unshuffles back to the codes;
  - selection: the lm_head keeps its method by default, the int4 method is selected on a mocked gfx1x device, and the option raises on other GPUs and on an already quantized head.
- gfx11/gfx12 GPU:
  - output matches a dequantized reference for 1, 4, 5, 6 and 32 tokens, which covers both the HIP and the Triton paths;
  - output stays close to the fp16/bf16 lm_head;
  - a tied lm_head leaves the input embedding in full precision.

**GSM8K, real int4 kernel** (lm-eval 0.4.13 `gsm8k_nothink`, 5-shot, first 100 questions, standard error about ±3.4 points):

| MoE backend | lm_head | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| Triton | fp16 | 88% | 88% |
| Triton | int4 g32 | 87% | 87% |
| `rdna3_w4a8` | fp16 | 89% | 88% |
| `rdna3_w4a8` | int4 g32 | 86% | 87% |

- **Changed answers:** 3 with Triton and 7 with `rdna3_w4a8`, all within noise. One of the `rdna3_w4a8` changes is formatting only ("16.00" for 16).
- **Full test set** (1,319 questions, lm_head fake-quantized to the same int4 g32 scheme): bf16 90.37% / 89.76%, int4 g32 90.30% / 90.07% (flexible / strict). This matches the published 90.2% for the uint4 g128 checkpoint.

**Token-level fidelity** (WikiText-2, 296,670 tokens, fake-quantized lm_head):

| lm_head | Perplexity | Change | Top-1 agreement with bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16, second run (noise floor) | 7.3725 | −0.02% | 98.14% |
| int4 g32 | 7.4282 | +0.74% | 94.58% |

int4 has a small, measurable token-level cost: perplexity rises 0.74%, and about 3.6% more top-1 tokens flip than the bf16 rerun does. It doesn't show up in GSM8K. That is why the option is opt-in rather than a default. A quality-neutral int8 per-channel format (perplexity +0.01%, top-1 99.34%) is proposed as a follow-up in [#63402](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63402), on top of this PR.

## Details

- **Scope:**
  - RDNA gfx11/gfx12 only, and only lm_heads that load unquantized.
  - There are no C++ changes: everything runs on ops already in `main`.
- **Not covered:**
  - LoRA and a separate `head_dtype` are rejected rather than supported.
  - Drafter lm_head copies keep their existing `draft_lm_head_quantization` handling.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - int8 per-channel lm_head ([#63402](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63402));
  - possibly int6 group 32, which matched llama.cpp's Q6_K accuracy (perplexity +0.07%, top-1 98.67%).

---

+
+import torch
+from torch.nn import Module, Parameter
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import UnquantizedLinearMethod
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.base_config import QuantizeMethodBase
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+    UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def _on_gfx1x() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1x
+
+    return on_gfx1x()
+
+
+class RdnaLMHeadMethod(QuantizeMethodBase):
+    """Loads the fp16/bf16 lm_head as usual, then replaces its weight with a
+    quantized copy run by an RDNA op.
+
+    A tied head only rebinds its own ``weight``, so the input embeddings keep
+    their full-precision weight.
+    """
+
+    scheme: ClassVar[str]
+    """The ``KernelConfig.lm_head_quantization`` value this method implements."""
+    n_align: ClassVar[int]
+    """Required divisor of the vocab shard (output rows)."""
+    k_align: ClassVar[int]
+    """Required divisor of the hidden size (input columns)."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self._unquantized = UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_config(
+        cls, quant_method: QuantizeMethodBase, vllm_config: "VllmConfig", prefix: str
+    ) -> Self:
+        """Check that ``lm_head_quantization`` can replace ``quant_method``."""
+        if not _on_gfx1x():
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization={cls.scheme!r} needs a ROCm gfx11 or gfx12 GPU."
+            )
+        if not isinstance(
+            quant_method, (UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod, UnquantizedLinearMethod)
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization needs an unquantized lm_head, but {prefix} "
+                f"uses {type(quant_method).__name__}."
+            )
+        model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+        if (
+            model_config is not None
+            and model_config.head_dtype is not None
+            and model_config.head_dtype != model_config.dtype
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "lm_head_quantization is not supported with a head_dtype that "
+                "differs from the model dtype."
+            )
+        if vllm_config.lora_config is not None:
+            raise ValueError("lm_head_quantization is not supported with LoRA.")
+        return cls()
+
+    def create_weights(self, layer: Module, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs):
+        self._unquantized.create_weights(layer, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs)
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: Module) -> None:
+        weight = layer.weight
+        n, k = weight.shape
+        if weight.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization needs an fp16/bf16 lm_head, got {weight.dtype}."
+            )
+        if n % self.n_align or k % self.k_align:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization={self.scheme!r} needs a vocab shard "
+                f"divisible by {self.n_align} and a hidden size divisible by "
+                f"{self.k_align}, got {n} x {k}."
+            )
+        self.quantize_weight(layer, weight.data)
+        logger.info_once(
+            "Quantized the lm_head to %s (%d x %d per rank).", self.scheme, n, k
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def set_weight(layer: Module, weight: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        """Register ``weight`` as a new ``layer.weight`` parameter.
+
+        Not `replace_parameter`, which keeps the loaded parameter and may copy
+        into its storage: a tied head shares both with the input embeddings, and
+        an untied head would keep its fp16 storage allocated.
+        """
+        layer.weight = Parameter(weight, requires_grad=False)
+

+        model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+        if (
+            model_config is not None
+            and model_config.head_dtype is not None
+            and model_config.head_dtype != model_config.dtype
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "lm_head_quantization is not supported with a head_dtype that "
+                "differs from the model dtype."
+            )
+        if vllm_config.lora_config is not None:
+            raise ValueError("lm_head_quantization is not supported with LoRA.")
+        return cls()
+
+    def create_weights(self, layer: Module, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs):
+        self._unquantized.create_weights(layer, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs)
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: Module) -> None:
+        weight = layer.weight
+        n, k = weight.shape
+        if weight.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization needs an fp16/bf16 lm_head, got {weight.dtype}."
+            )
+        if n % self.n_align or k % self.k_align:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization={self.scheme!r} needs a vocab shard "
+                f"divisible by {self.n_align} and a hidden size divisible by "
+                f"{self.k_align}, got {n} x {k}."

detail.body:
## Overview

This PR adds an opt-in `KernelConfig.lm_head_quantization` option for RDNA (ROCm gfx11/gfx12). With `"int4_per_group_32"`, an unquantized fp16/bf16 lm_head is quantized while the model loads:

- asymmetric uint4 weights;
- one scale and zero point per 32 input channels.

The quantized lm_head runs on the existing RDNA hybrid W4A16 op (`rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply`): `wvSplitK_int4_g` for decode (up to 5 tokens) and the Triton W4A16 kernel for prefill.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --kernel-config '{"lm_head_quantization": "int4_per_group_32"}'
```

**Why.** Decode reads the whole lm_head every step. Many int4 checkpoints keep it in full precision, so on bandwidth-bound RDNA GPUs it becomes one of the largest per-token costs. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Quark UINT4 group 128) is one example:

- Its 248320 × 2048 fp16 lm_head is about 970 MB, read every token: 4.5 ms at 211 GB/s on Strix Halo (gfx1151), the largest single item in decode.
- llama.cpp's Q4_K_M GGUF of the same model stores it as Q6_K.

Quantizing at load time needs no new checkpoint and no new kernel.

**Design.**

- **New method:** `Int4LMHeadMethod` (`quantization/online/int4_lm_head.py`) creates the weight like `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, so checkpoint loading does not change. In `process_weights_after_loading` it:
  - quantizes the weight in row chunks, which bounds the fp32 working set;
  - widens each group's range to include 0;
  - writes the codes in the layout `wvSplitK_int4_g` expects (ExLlama-shuffled int4, padded off the vector-cache cliff on gfx1151);
  - writes packed zero points `[N/8, K/32]`.
- **Shared layout code:** `pack_skinny_int4` is split, so `skinny_int4_layout` (the gfx1151 padding step) can be reused on already-shuffled weights.
- **Hook:** `ParallelLMHead` calls `_maybe_quantize_lm_head` only when no quant method was preselected, so the drafter lm_head copies made by `quantized_lm_head_copy` are not affected. The method class is imported lazily.
- **Tied embeddings:** `replace_parameter` rebinds only the lm_head's `weight`, so tied input embeddings keep their full-precision weight. An untied head frees its fp16 weight; a tied head adds the int4 copy (about 0.29 GB at this size) on top of the shared embedding.
- **Errors:** the option raises `ValueError` when it can't apply:
  - a GPU other than gfx11/gfx12;
  - an lm_head that is already quantized;
  - a `head_dtype` different from the model dtype;
  - LoRA;
  - a vocab shard not divisible by 8, or a hidden size not divisible by 32.

  It never falls back silently. The default (`None`) changes nothing.

## Claims

Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, 40 CUs, LPDDR5X about 211 GB/s), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Quark UINT4-G128 (fp16 lm_head, 248320 × 2048). Decode benchmark: 512 input / 512 output tokens, batch size 1, greedy, `ignore_eos`, median of 5 runs after 3 warmups, CUDA graphs on (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`).

| MoE backend | lm_head | TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Triton (default) | fp16 | 29.76 | 33.6 | |
| Triton (default) | **int4 g32 (this PR)** | **26.66** | **37.5** | −3.10 ms, 1.12x |
| `rdna3_w4a8` ([#62480](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62480)) | fp16 | 20.69 | 48.3 | |
| `rdna3_w4a8` ([#62480](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62480)) | **int4 g32 (this PR)** | **17.50** | **57.1** | −3.19 ms, 1.18x |

- **Saving vs bandwidth math:** the measured 3.1 to 3.2 ms/token saving matches the expected value. The lm_head read drops from about 970 MB to about 300 MB per token, about 3.2 ms at 211 GB/s.
- **Weight memory:** 18.51 GiB → 17.87 GiB.
- **Run variance:** in the combined run, 4 of 5 runs were 17.47 to 17.53 ms; one outlier at 19.53 ms doesn't change the median.
- **llama.cpp reference:** llama.cpp (Q4_K_M, `llama-bench` tg512) measures 17.82 ms on the same machine. The combined configuration is the first vLLM setup to match it on this model.

**Accuracy:** GSM8K is unchanged within noise. There is a small token-level cost, measured below.

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_int4_lm_head.py`

- CPU:
  - quantization error is at most one step, with a bounded RMS error (fp16 and bf16);
  - zero-point packing round-trips;
  - the packed layout unshuffles back to the codes;
  - selection: the lm_head keeps its method by default, the int4 method is selected on a mocked gfx1x device, and the option raises on other GPUs and on an already quantized head.
- gfx11/gfx12 GPU:
  - output matches a dequantized reference for 1, 4, 5, 6 and 32 tokens, which covers both the HIP and the Triton paths;
  - output stays close to the fp16/bf16 lm_head;
  - a tied lm_head leaves the input embedding in full precision.

**GSM8K, real int4 kernel** (lm-eval 0.4.13 `gsm8k_nothink`, 5-shot, first 100 questions, standard error about ±3.4 points):

| MoE backend | lm_head | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| Triton | fp16 | 88% | 88% |
| Triton | int4 g32 | 87% | 87% |
| `rdna3_w4a8` | fp16 | 89% | 88% |
| `rdna3_w4a8` | int4 g32 | 86% | 87% |

- **Changed answers:** 3 with Triton and 7 with `rdna3_w4a8`, all within noise. One of the `rdna3_w4a8` changes is formatting only ("16.00" for 16).
- **Full test set** (1,319 questions, lm_head fake-quantized to the same int4 g32 scheme): bf16 90.37% / 89.76%, int4 g32 90.30% / 90.07% (flexible / strict). This matches the published 90.2% for the uint4 g128 checkpoint.

**Token-level fidelity** (WikiText-2, 296,670 tokens, fake-quantized lm_head):

| lm_head | Perplexity | Change | Top-1 agreement with bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16, second run (noise floor) | 7.3725 | −0.02% | 98.14% |
| int4 g32 | 7.4282 | +0.74% | 94.58% |

int4 has a small, measurable token-level cost: perplexity rises 0.74%, and about 3.6% more top-1 tokens flip than the bf16 rerun does. It doesn't show up in GSM8K. That is why the option is opt-in rather than a default. A quality-neutral int8 per-channel format (perplexity +0.01%, top-1 99.34%) is proposed as a follow-up in [#63402](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63402), on top of this PR.

## Details

- **Scope:**
  - RDNA gfx11/gfx12 only, and only lm_heads that load unquantized.
  - There are no C++ changes: everything runs on ops already in `main`.
- **Not covered:**
  - LoRA and a separate `head_dtype` are rejected rather than supported.
  - Drafter lm_head copies keep their existing `draft_lm_head_quantization` handling.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - int8 per-channel lm_head ([#63402](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63402));
  - possibly int6 group 32, which matched llama.cpp's Q6_K accuracy (perplexity +0.07%, top-1 98.67%).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for the load-time lm_head quantization (KernelConfig.lm_head_quantization).
+
+Tests shared by every scheme are parametrized over ``SCHEMES``; the
+quantizer tests of each scheme follow them.
+
+Run `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_lm_head.py`.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import KernelConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mixed_precision import rdna_hybrid_w4a16
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import UnquantizedLinearMethod
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.online import rdna_lm_head
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.online.int4_lm_head import (
+    GROUP_SIZE,
+    Int4LMHeadMethod,
+    pack_zero_points,
+    quantize_int4_rows,
+    quantize_lm_head_int4,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.online.rdna_lm_head import (
+    RdnaLMHeadMethod,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+    ParallelLMHead,
+    UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod,
+    VocabParallelEmbedding,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+# Not a multiple of the vocab padding, so the head has zero-filled rows.
+VOCAB, HIDDEN = 4000, 2048
+
+
+def _on_gfx1x() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1x
+
+    return on_gfx1x()
+
+
+requires_gfx1x = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _on_gfx1x(), reason="The RDNA lm_head ops are gfx11/gfx12 only"
+)
+
+
+def _dequantize_int4(codes, scales, zero_points, group_size=GROUP_SIZE):
+    scale = scales.float().repeat_interleave(group_size, dim=1)
+    zero_point = zero_points.float().repeat_interleave(group_size, dim=1)
+    return (codes.float() - zero_point) * scale
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scheme:
+    method: type[RdnaLMHeadMethod]
+    reference: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor]
+    """Full-precision weight -> the fp32 weight the kernel should compute with."""
+    weight_dtype: torch.dtype
+    weight_cols: Callable[[int], int]
+    """Hidden size -> columns of the stored weight."""
+    full_precision_tol: float
+    """Bound on the relative error against the unquantized head."""
+
+    @property
+    def name(self) -> str:
+        return self.method.scheme
+
+
+SCHEMES = [
+    pytest.param(
+        Scheme(
+            method=Int4LMHeadMethod,
+            reference=lambda w: _dequantize_int4(*quantize_int4_rows(w)),
+            weight_dtype=torch.int8,
+            weight_cols=lambda k: k // 2,
+            full_precision_tol=0.12,
+        ),
+        id="int4_per_group_32",
+    ),
+]
+
+
+def _config(scheme: Scheme) -> VllmConfig:
+    return VllmConfig(kernel_config=KernelConfig(lm_head_quantization=scheme.name))
+
+
+def test_lm_head_keeps_its_method_by_default():
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+        head = ParallelLMHead(VOCAB, HIDDEN, disable_tp=True)
+    assert isinstance(head.quant_method, UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheme", SCHEMES)
+def test_lm_head_quantization_selects_method(scheme, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rdna_lm_head, "_on_gfx1x", lambda: True)
+    with set_current_vllm_config(_config(scheme)):
+        head = ParallelLMHead(VOCAB, HIDDEN, disable_tp=True)
+        embed = VocabParallelEmbedding(VOCAB, HIDDEN, disable_tp=True)
+    assert type(head.quant_method) is scheme.method
+    # Only the lm_head is quantized.
+    assert isinstance(embed.quant_method, UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheme", SCHEMES)
+def test_lm_head_quantization_rejects_other_gpus(scheme, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rdna_lm_head, "_on_gfx1x", lambda: False)
+    with (
+        set_current_vllm_config(_config(scheme)),
+        pytest.raises(ValueError, match="gfx11 or gfx12"),
+    ):
+        ParallelLMHead(VOCAB, HIDDEN, disable_tp=True)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheme", SCHEMES)
+def test_lm_head_quantization_rejects_quantized_head(scheme, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rdna_lm_head, "_on_gfx1x", lambda: True)
+    config = _config(scheme)
+    # A checkpoint that excludes the lm_head hands out UnquantizedLinearMethod.
+    assert isinstance(
+        scheme.method.from_config(UnquantizedLinearMethod(), config, "lm_head"),
+        scheme.method,
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unquantized lm_head"):
+        scheme.method.from_config(scheme.method(), config, "lm_head")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheme", SCHEMES)
+def test_lm_head_quantization_rejects_head_dtype_and_lora(scheme, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rdna_lm_head, "_on_gfx1x", lambda: True)
+    # from_config only reads these attributes of the VllmConfig.
+    model_config = SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.bfloat16, head_dtype=torch.float32)
+    config = SimpleNamespace(model_config=model_config, lora_config=None)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="head_dtype"):
+        scheme.method.from_config(UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod(), config, "lm_head")
+
+    model_config.head_dtype = None
+    config.lora_config = object()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="LoRA"):
+        scheme.method.from_config(UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod(), config, "lm_head")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheme", SCHEMES)
+def test_lm_head_quantization_rejects_bad_weights(scheme, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rdna_lm_head, "_on_gfx1x", lambda: True)
+    hidden = HIDDEN + scheme.method.k_align // 2
+    with set_current_vllm_config(_config(scheme)):
+        head = ParallelLMHead(
+            VOCAB, hidden, disable_tp=True, params_dtype=torch.float32
+        )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="fp16/bf16"):
+        head.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(head)
+
+    head = head.to(torch.bfloat16)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=f"divisible by {scheme.method.k_align}"):
+        head.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(head)
+
+
+def _loaded_head(
+    scheme: Scheme, dtype: torch.dtype, tie: bool = False, device: str = "cuda"
+):
+    with set_current_vllm_config(_config(scheme)):
+        head = ParallelLMHead(VOCAB, HIDDEN, disable_tp=True)
+        embed = VocabParallelEmbedding(VOCAB, HIDDEN, disable_tp=True)
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    for layer in (head, embed):
+        layer.weight.data.copy_(torch.randn(layer.weight.shape, generator=gen) * 0.02)
+    if tie:
+        head = head.tie_weights(embed)
+    return head.to(device, dtype), embed.to(device, dtype)
+
+
+@requires_gfx1x
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheme", SCHEMES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 4, 5, 6, 32, 256])
+def test_lm_head_matches_reference(scheme, dtype, num_tokens):
+    head, _ = _loaded_head(scheme, dtype)
+    weight = head.weight.detach().clone()
+    reference = scheme.reference(weight)
+    head.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(head)
+
+    assert head.weight.dtype == scheme.weight_dtype
+    assert head.weight.shape == (weight.shape[0], scheme.weight_cols(HIDDEN))
+
+    torch.manual_seed(1)
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    out = head.quant_method.apply(head, x).float()
+    assert out.shape == (num_tokens, weight.shape[0])
+
+    ref = x.float() @ reference.t()
+    assert ((out - ref).norm() / ref.norm()).item() < 1e-2
+
+    full = x.float() @ weight.float().t()
+    assert ((out - full).norm() / full.norm()).item() < scheme.full_precision_tol
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheme", SCHEMES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tie", [False, True], ids=["untied", "tied"])
+def test_quantized_head_does_not_reuse_loaded_weight(scheme, tie, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rdna_lm_head, "_on_gfx1x", lambda: True)
+    # Without the gfx1151 row padding the quantized weight is contiguous, the
+    # case where reusing the loaded storage would overwrite it.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rdna_hybrid_w4a16, "_on_gfx1151", lambda: False)
+    head, embed = _loaded_head(scheme, torch.bfloat16, tie=tie, device="cpu")
+    loaded = head.weight
+    embed_weight = embed.weight.detach().clone()
+    head.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(head)
+
+    assert head.weight is not loaded
+    assert head.weight.dtype == scheme.weight_dtype
+    assert (
+        head.weight.untyped_storage().data_ptr() != loaded.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+    )
+    # A tied head shares the embedding's weight until it is quantized.
+    assert embed.weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert torch.equal(embed.weight, embed_weight)
+
+
+# int4_per_group_32 quantizer
+
+
+def _unshuffle(w_q: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Invert the ExLlama shuffle: int8 [N, K // 2] -> uint4 codes [N, K]."""
+    words = w_q.view(torch.int32)
+    shifts = torch.tensor([0, 16, 4, 20, 8, 24, 12, 28], dtype=torch.int32)
+    codes = (words.unsqueeze(-1) >> shifts.to(words.device)) & 0xF
+    return codes.reshape(words.shape[0], -1).to(torch.uint8)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_quantize_int4_rows_error_bound(dtype):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    weight = (torch.randn(64, 256) * 0.02).to(dtype)
+    weight[-8:] = 0  # vocab padding rows
+    codes, scales, zero_points = quantize_int4_rows(weight)
+
+    assert codes.shape == (64, 256) and codes.dtype == torch.uint8
+    assert scales.shape == (64, 256 // GROUP_SIZE) and scales.dtype == dtype
+    assert int(codes.max()) <= 15 and int(zero_points.max()) <= 15
+
+    dequant = _dequantize_int4(codes, scales, zero_points)
+    error = dequant - weight.float()
+    # Rounding the zero point can clip a group's endpoint by up to half a step.
+    step = scales.float().repeat_interleave(GROUP_SIZE, dim=1)
+    assert (error.abs() <= step).all()
+    assert (error.norm() / weight.float().norm()).item() < 0.1
+    assert torch.equal(dequant[-8:], torch.zeros(8, 256))
+
+
+def test_pack_zero_points_roundtrip():
+    zero_points = torch.randint(0, 16, (64, 8), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    words = pack_zero_points(zero_points)
+    assert words.shape == (8, 8) and words.dtype == torch.int32
+    shifts = (torch.arange(64) % 8 * 4).view(64, 1).to(torch.int32)
+    unpacked = (words.repeat_interleave(8, dim=0) >> shifts) & 0xF
+    assert torch.equal(unpacked.to(torch.uint8), zero_points)
+
+
+def test_quantize_lm_head_int4_layout():
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    weight = (torch.randn(96, 128) * 0.02).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    w_q, w_s, w_zp = quantize_lm_head_int4(weight, chunk_rows=40)
+    codes, scales, zero_points = quantize_int4_rows(weight)
+
+    assert w_q.dtype == torch.int8 and w_q.shape == (96, 64)
+    assert torch.equal(_unshuffle(w_q), codes)
+    assert torch.equal(w_s, scales)
+    assert torch.equal(w_zp, pack_zero_points(zero_points))

+quantizes every other linear layer. ``Int4LMHeadMethod`` quantizes the loaded
+weight to asymmetric uint4 with one scale and zero point per 32 input channels
+and runs it on the RDNA hybrid W4A16 op (HIP skinny GEMM for decode, Triton
+for prefill).

+
+import torch
+from torch.nn import Module, Parameter
+
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mixed_precision.rdna_hybrid_w4a16 import (
+    pack_int4_exllama_shuffle,
+    skinny_int4_layout,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.online.rdna_lm_head import (
+    RdnaLMHeadMethod,
+)
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import num_compute_units
+
+GROUP_SIZE = 32
+_UINT4_MAX = 15
+
+
+def quantize_int4_rows(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, group_size: int = GROUP_SIZE
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Asymmetric uint4 quantization of the rows of ``weight`` [N, K].
+
+    Returns the codes [N, K] uint8, the scales [N, K // group_size] in the
+    weight dtype and the zero points [N, K // group_size] uint8, such that
+    ``(codes - zero_point) * scale`` approximates ``weight``. Each group's range
+    is widened to include 0, so the zero point always fits in uint4.
+    """
+    n, k = weight.shape
+    groups = weight.float().view(n, k // group_size, group_size)
+    w_min = groups.amin(dim=-1).clamp(max=0)
+    w_max = groups.amax(dim=-1).clamp(min=0)
+    # Quantize against the stored scale so the kernel dequantizes exactly the
+    # values the codes were rounded for.
+    scale = (
+        ((w_max - w_min) / _UINT4_MAX)
+        .clamp(min=torch.finfo(weight.dtype).tiny)
+        .to(weight.dtype)
+    )
+    scale_f = scale.float()
+    zero_point = (-w_min / scale_f).round().clamp(0, _UINT4_MAX)
+    codes = ((groups / scale_f.unsqueeze(-1)).round() + zero_point.unsqueeze(-1)).clamp(
+        0, _UINT4_MAX
+    )
+    return (
+        codes.to(torch.uint8).view(n, k),
+        scale,
+        zero_point.to(torch.uint8),
+    )
+
+
+def pack_zero_points(zero_point: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Pack uint4 zero points along rows: [N, G] -> [N // 8, G] int32.
+
+    Row n lands in word n // 8 at bits 4 * (n % 8).
+    """
+    n, g = zero_point.shape
+    shifts = torch.arange(0, 32, 4, dtype=torch.int32, device=zero_point.device)
+    words = zero_point.to(torch.int32).view(n // 8, 8, g) << shifts.view(1, 8, 1)
+    # The nibbles are disjoint, so the (wrapping) sum is their bitwise OR.
+    return words.sum(dim=1, dtype=torch.int32)

+        super().__init__()

+        """Check that ``lm_head_quantization`` can replace ``quant_method``."""
+        if not _on_gfx1x():
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization={cls.scheme!r} needs a ROCm gfx11 or gfx12 GPU."
+            )
+        if not isinstance(
+            quant_method, (UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod, UnquantizedLinearMethod)
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization needs an unquantized lm_head, but {prefix} "
+                f"uses {type(quant_method).__name__}."
+            )
+        model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+        if (
+            model_config is not None
+            and model_config.head_dtype is not None

+                "lm_head_quantization is not supported with a head_dtype that "
+                "differs from the model dtype."

+        if vllm_config.lora_config is not None:
+            raise ValueError("lm_head_quantization is not supported with LoRA.")
+        return cls()
+
+    def create_weights(self, layer: Module, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs):
+        self._unquantized.create_weights(layer, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs)
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: Module) -> None:
+        weight = layer.weight
+        n, k = weight.shape
+        if weight.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization needs an fp16/bf16 lm_head, got {weight.dtype}."
+            )
+        if n % self.n_align or k % self.k_align:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization={self.scheme!r} needs a vocab shard "
+                f"divisible by {self.n_align} and a hidden size divisible by "
+                f"{self.k_align}, got {n} x {k}."
+            )
+        self.quantize_weight(layer, weight.data)
+        logger.info_once(
+            "Quantized the lm_head to %s (%d x %d per rank).", self.scheme, n, k
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def set_weight(layer: Module, weight: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        """Register ``weight`` as a new ``layer.weight`` parameter.
+
+        Not `replace_parameter`, which keeps the loaded parameter and may copy
+        into its storage: a tied head shares both with the input embeddings, and
+        an untied head would keep its fp16 storage allocated.
+        """
+        layer.weight = Parameter(weight, requires_grad=False)

+    @abstractmethod
+    def quantize_weight(self, layer: Module, weight: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        """Replace ``layer.weight`` with the quantized copy of ``weight`` (via
+        `set_weight`) and register any scale tensors the op needs."""
+        raise NotImplementedError

+    @abstractmethod
+    def matmul(

+    ) -> torch.Tensor:

+        raise NotImplementedError

+        self, layer: Module, x: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:

+        output = self.matmul(layer, x_2d, bias)
+        return output.reshape(*x.shape[:-1], output.shape[-1])

+

+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, ClassVar, Self
+
+import torch
+from torch.nn import Module, Parameter
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import UnquantizedLinearMethod
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.base_config import QuantizeMethodBase
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+    UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def _on_gfx1x() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1x
+
+    return on_gfx1x()
+
+
+class RdnaLMHeadMethod(QuantizeMethodBase):
+    """Loads the fp16/bf16 lm_head as usual, then replaces its weight with a
+    quantized copy run by an RDNA op.
+
+    A tied head only rebinds its own ``weight``, so the input embeddings keep
+    their full-precision weight.
+    """
+
+    scheme: ClassVar[str]
+    """The ``KernelConfig.lm_head_quantization`` value this method implements."""
+    n_align: ClassVar[int]
+    """Required divisor of the vocab shard (output rows)."""
+    k_align: ClassVar[int]
+    """Required divisor of the hidden size (input columns)."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self._unquantized = UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_config(
+        cls, quant_method: QuantizeMethodBase, vllm_config: "VllmConfig", prefix: str
+    ) -> Self:
+        """Check that ``lm_head_quantization`` can replace ``quant_method``."""
+        if not _on_gfx1x():
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization={cls.scheme!r} needs a ROCm gfx11 or gfx12 GPU."
+            )
+        if not isinstance(
+            quant_method, (UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod, UnquantizedLinearMethod)
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization needs an unquantized lm_head, but {prefix} "
+                f"uses {type(quant_method).__name__}."
+            )
+        model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+        if (
+            model_config is not None
+            and model_config.head_dtype is not None
+            and model_config.head_dtype != model_config.dtype
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "lm_head_quantization is not supported with a head_dtype that "
+                "differs from the model dtype."
+            )
+        if vllm_config.lora_config is not None:
+            raise ValueError("lm_head_quantization is not supported with LoRA.")
+        return cls()
+
+    def create_weights(self, layer: Module, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs):
+        self._unquantized.create_weights(layer, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs)
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: Module) -> None:
+        weight = layer.weight
+        n, k = weight.shape
+        if weight.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization needs an fp16/bf16 lm_head, got {weight.dtype}."
+            )
+        if n % self.n_align or k % self.k_align:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"lm_head_quantization={self.scheme!r} needs a vocab shard "
+                f"divisible by {self.n_align} and a hidden size divisible by "
+                f"{self.k_align}, got {n} x {k}."
